For in the treasury of the Caliph there was not even a single dinar at that time;
rather, that Caliph al-Muqtafi had ten thousand dinars before he became ruler,
and with them he supplied his needs upon his accession to the throne.
And the proclamation of al-Rashid and Sultan Dawud ceased,
and that of al-Muqtafi and Sultan Mas'ud was established.
It is said
that when the Sultan left the court of the Caliph,
he summoned the vizier to him,
and reproached him for his choice,
and said:
"You have acted foolishly in that you set up a mature man,
middle-aged,
intelligent.
If you had set up a young boy and reared him,
he would have looked upon you with favor,
and the command and administration of the realm would have remained in your hands for a long time,
until he attained full stature.
Believe me, believe me,
you will not hold out long with this chosen one of yours,
and you will see!"
And when the year five hundred and thirty-one entered,
531 of the Arabs [1136-1137 AD]:
the son of Danishmend, the lord of Melitene, sent an envoy to the Sultan in Baghdad,
to persuade him not to attack his territory again {OCR?}.
And when they brought the envoy to kiss the threshold, as was customary,
he contended and refused,
and said:
"I will not kiss a threshold whose master has been expelled from it."
Now Zengi gathered an army and came as far as Tikrit,
and he fell upon the herd of Sultan Mas'ud,
and returned to Mosul.
Then Caliph al-Muqtafi sent to Zengi,
and promised to give him ten renowned places,
provided that he would not help al-Rashid.
Zengi, however, replied:
"I have sworn oaths that I will not surrender him into your hands.
Truly, if you give me these places,
I will proclaim you, and I will be at peace,
and I will not assist this one;
yet from my presence I will not expel him."
And ten places were given to him,
among them Harbi, Hasiyrah, Sarifayn, Hillah, and the rest.
And Zengi proclaimed al-Muqtafi and Sultan Mas'ud.
And he lodged al-Rashid near him, in the palace called 'of Gold' in Mosul.
